# The Massachusetts SNAP sheet against the twin of 7 USC 2017(a)

*Generated by crosscheck/snap_crosscheck.pl. For each household the sheet engine computes the Massachusetts sheet (MLRI, October 2026); its deductions are given to the RuleSpec twin of 7 USC 2017(a) (LE2 examples/migration/rulespec/snap) with the calculation date 1 October 2026, and the allotments are compared.*

The twin's maximum-allotment tables run to fiscal year 2026 (from 1 October 2025): the corpus it was built from (rulespec-us at the commit corpus.pl pins) has not yet published the fiscal year 2027 adjustment the sheet uses (one person: $306 against $298). Where only that table differs, the allotments differ by the same amount.

The rounding is a finding about the sheet: the federal rules round 30% of net income up to the next dollar and the allotment down (7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)), and the RuleSpec twin, read from the statute and its tests, does; the Massachusetts calculator keeps the cents, so its estimate can exceed the benefit by up to one dollar. The homeless case shows the sheet relying on its user: it computes a shelter deduction whenever utilities are entered, and its note tells a homeless household to skip that step.

Not compared here: the PolicyEngine twin (lpsPlus examples/migration/policyengine/snap), whose cases describe each person of a household with some sixty facts; see the review report.
